listing_view.reasoning: Revenue momentum (29.2% latest-year growth) and a fast-growing SaaS line (₹1,036M to ₹2,043M over two years [business, page 228]) give bankers a good story to sell, and the tiny ₹32 price band suggests a retail-accessible listing. But I have zero demand-side data — no subscription, anchor, GMP or broker inputs were collected — so anything above or below 'slightly cautious' would be invented.

longterm_view.reasoning: The business has never generated a rupee of operating cash: -548, -273, -18 across three years, and the improvement of the burn is the best thing about it. Asset-light claims (no inventory [business, page 244], all-leased premises [business, page 253]) make persistent cash burn worse, not better — there is no capex story to hide behind. My view is wrong if FY2027 turns OCF positive and SaaS keeps compounding near the ~40% pace implied by [business, page 228].

governance.reasoning: There are criminal proceedings against Promoters/Directors Kunal Bahl and Rohit Kumar Bansal per the company's own litigation chapter [litigation, page 477]; the extract cuts off before the nature or severity is shown, which is itself a red flag, not an exoneration. The boilerplate on arm's-length related-party dealings [promoters, page 370] does not offset that.

key_risks.why_it_matters: Three consecutive years of cash burn (-548, -273, -18 ₹M) means the listing proceeds are funding operations, and no extract given to me explains why this changes.

The prospectus itself directs readers to criminal proceedings against the two promoter-directors, and the extract provided truncates before disclosing substance, so the risk is real but unquantifiable from what I was given.

answers.question: Our reading triggered a hard stop: negative operating cash flow in all three years. Is there an explanation in the document?
answers.answer: Not in what I was given. No extract addresses why operating cash flow was negative in FY2024 (-548.45), FY2025 (-273.47) or FY2026 (-17.97), and no cash-flow chapter extract was provided at all. The only circumstantial context: the company claims an inventory-free, no-owned-premises model [business, page 244], [business, page 253], which removes the usual capex/working-capital excuses and makes the burn harder to explain away; the trajectory is improving sharply, but improving burn is still burn. Treat the hard stop as unresolved on this evidence.

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: A cash-flow-statement extract showing working-capital timing (e.g., receivable build) rather than genuine losses behind the negative OCF, plus the full text of the promoter criminal proceedings [litigation, page 477], would move both scores meaningfully — up if benign, down sharply if not.
